cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's just shown them that Christ has indeed been raised from the dead (1 Corinthians 15:20). Now he sees the next question coming: "How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?"
Paul starts his answer with two words: "You fool!" No warm-up and no "great question, friend," just straight out to a farmer's field to watch what happens to the seed.

cards.question: Out in the field, Paul says what you sow does not come to life unless it ___.
Paul says the seed you put in the ground already looks like the plant that will grow from it.
A little seed of wheat goes in the ground. Who does Paul say gives it the body it comes up with?

cards.text: God gives every kind of seed its own body, just as He designed it. Friend, nobody pulls a tray out of my oven yelling, "HEY! Where did my little dough ball GO?"

cards.question: Next Paul looks at men, animals, birds and fish. What does he say about their flesh?

answers.text: Men and animals share one kind

cards.text: Now Paul looks up. There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, he says, and their splendor is not the same degree.

cards.question: Up in the sky, Paul says the sun, the moon and every single star all share the same splendor.

cards.text: Seed. Flesh. Sun. Moon. STARS. And then Paul lands it: "So will it be with the resurrection of the dead".

cards.question: Paul says the body that is sown is perishable. How does he say it is raised?
Paul keeps going, pair by pair. It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in ___. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in ___.

cards.text: Baker, I went into that junk drawer with my edges worn down to nothing, so "raised in power" has my mustache doing a LITTLE DANCE. Paul has one more pair, and it starts like this: it is sown a natural body.

cards.question: Paul says it is sown a natural body. What kind of body does he say it is raised?

cards.text: Then Paul goes all the way back to the very first man. It is written: "The first man Adam became a living being".

cards.question: After the first man Adam, Paul says there is also a last Adam. What does Paul call the last Adam?
Paul says the spiritual came first, and the natural came after it.

cards.text: The first man was of the dust of the earth, and those who are of the earth are like him. Baker, I spent YEARS under dust in that junk drawer, so I'm not saying one word against dust.

cards.question: The first man was of the dust of the earth. Where does Paul say the second man is from?
Paul says we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, and so also we shall bear the likeness of the ___ man.
Paul tells the brothers that flesh and blood can inherit the kingdom of God just as it is.

cards.text: Then Paul leans in close: "Listen, I tell you a mystery". Not all of us will sleep, he says.

cards.question: Paul's mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be ___.
How fast does Paul say this change happens?

answers.text: In the twinkling of an eye

cards.text: It happens at the last trumpet, when the dead will be raised imperishable and we will be changed. The twinkling of an eye, baker. It takes me longer than that to FIND MY APRON!

cards.question: Paul says the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with ___.

cards.text: And when that clothing change is done, Paul says, a saying that is written will come to pass.

cards.question: What does that written saying say happens to death?

answers.text: It is swallowed up in victory
It is put off for a while

cards.text: Then Paul talks straight to death. To DEATH, baker, face to face: "Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?"

cards.question: Paul says death has a sting, and the sting of death is ___.
Paul says we win the victory over death by our own strength.

cards.text: So now what? Paul tells his beloved brothers to be steadfast and immovable and always excel in the work of the Lord, which in my bakery means KEEP THOSE OVENS HOT.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers to always excel in the work of the Lord. Why?

answers.text: Their labor in the Lord is not in vain
The work is nearly finished now
They will be paid in full this life

findings.problem: The card tells "raised in power" from 1 Corinthians 15:43 as well as the start of 15:44, but it cites only 1 Corinthians 15:44. The citation should be 1 Corinthians 15:43-44.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer "Imperishable" is one Bible-sounding word. The wrong answers are longer, plainer phrases ("Exactly the same as before", "Partly restored"), so the right answer stands out by its length and tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: The question asks "How fast does Paul say this change happens?" "This change" points back to the previous choice card, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the change is, for example that we will all be changed.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks "What does that written saying say happens to death?" "That written saying" points back to story card 13, which is no longer on screen. The question should give its own context, for example that once the perishable is clothed with the imperishable, a written saying comes to pass.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer "It is swallowed up in victory" sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers "It is put off for a while" and "It becomes a little gentler" sound casual and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: In the BSB, 1 Corinthians 15:55 is set in quotation marks right after "the saying that is written" (15:54), so it is presented as a written saying. The card presents it as Paul himself talking "straight to death," and it adds "face to face," which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions sin, so the baker has nothing to reason from when choosing "sin" over "fear" or "pain." The card also asks the baker to fill in the wording of the line rather than its meaning. As written, this is a guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The second half of 1 Corinthians 15:56, "the power of sin is the law," is never told on any card. The baker leaves without this part of Paul's point.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The climax of 1 Corinthians 15:57 is that God gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. No story card ever tells it. The baker only meets it indirectly, by marking the statement "by our own strength" as false, so they never hear who gives the victory or through whom.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer "Their labor in the Lord is not in vain" uses Bible phrasing. The wrong answers are plainer, and "They will be paid in full this life" is awkwardly worded (it is missing "in"). The right answer stands out as the only one that sounds like Scripture.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
